core_obligations: Define Y' as the normalization and transfer (2)(4)(5).
Prove the permanence properties of f'.
difficulty_reason: For f : X -> Y universally closed and quasi-separated between spaces over S, the lemma builds X -> Y' -> Y with f' universally closed, quasi-compact, quasi-separated and SURJECTIVE, pi integral, f'_*O_X = O_{Y'}, Y' = Spec_Y(f_*O_X) the normalization of Y in X, and proves the construction commutes with flat base change. The retained proof is complete: existence (2),(4),(5) is the chapter's normalization definition with its three cited lemmas; f' inherits universally closed / qc / qs by the permanence chain; the surjectivity argument is written out affinely — Y = Spec R, Y' = Spec A with A = Gamma(X, O_X) integral over R, the image V(I) closed, any h in I restricts to a nowhere-nonvanishing global section on qc X hence nilpotent, but A IS the section ring so h is nilpotent, I sits in the Jacobson radical and V(I) = Y'; flat-base-change compatibility is cited to the same normalization lemmas. Retained author proof at lines 8019-8058.
